literal: An edict ordered Yong to follow Prince Jian of Shun in Qi Commandery in the Taihe precedent: after audience, led to a seat, with special exemption from bowing and prostration.
idiomatic: An edict had Yong follow the Taihe precedent of Prince Jian of Shun in Qi Commandery—after court he was seated and spared the full bowing rites.

literal: He took charge within and without, and with Yuan Cha jointly decided ordinary government.
idiomatic: He oversaw affairs inside and outside the palace and ruled day-to-day government with Yuan Cha.

literal: Annual stipend exceeded ten thousand, grain reached forty thousand, performing girls filled the chambers, his sons wore eunuch caps and princely robes, and the splendor of rank and wealth no brother could match.
idiomatic: His yearly income ran past ten thousand, his grain allowance to forty thousand; performers crowded his halls, his sons went in court dress, and none of his brothers matched his glory.

literal: After his principal consort Lady Lu died, he took in again the younger sister of Cui Xian of Boling, who was greatly favored for her beauty; he wished to make her princess consort.
idiomatic: When his chief consort, Lady Lu, died, he took Cui Xian of Boling's younger sister, favored for her beauty, and meant to raise her to princess consort.

literal: At first Emperor Xiaozong, because the Cui clan was in the age called "Eastern Cui," of low estate and weak standing, found it difficult, and only after long delay permitted it.
idiomatic: At first Xiaozong hesitated: the Cuis were known as "Eastern Cui," of humble birth and slight prestige; only after long delay did he consent.

literal: After Yanming, he often favored singing girls and attendants, nearly a hundred persons, while casting aside Lady Cui, who was confined in a separate quarter and barred from affairs within, receiving only food and clothing.
idiomatic: After Yanming he kept nearly a hundred singing girls and attendants, while Lady Cui was shut in a side quarter, shut out of household rule, and given only food and clothes.

literal: So far that at his side there were again no maidservants; if his children wished to visit their mother, they had to report and request leave, and only when permitted might they see her.
idiomatic: In time he kept no maids at all; his children had to petition before they might see their mother, and only on permission were they admitted.

literal: Before long Lady Cui died suddenly; many said Yong had beaten her to death.
idiomatic: Soon Lady Cui died suddenly; many whispered Yong had beaten her to death.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling had promised to grant him her singing girls, but before they were sent Yong sent his eunuch Ding E himself into the palace, selected four mouths, and falsely claimed them back to his residence.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling had promised him her singing girls, but before they were sent Yong's eunuch Ding E entered the palace, picked four, and carried them off to his house under false pretense.

literal: The empress dowager rebuked his usurpation and ordered it stopped and recalled.
idiomatic: The empress dowager rebuked his presumption and had the grant halted and the women recalled.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang an edict said: "Of late the chancellor's office has not been opened, and yin and yang have not shifted.
idiomatic: Early in Xiaochang an edict read: "Of late the chancellor's gates have stayed shut and the seasons have not turned.

literal: The prince, holding wisdom within the clan, of heavy merit and standing, shields the black-haired people in the Way, his might reaching the Hua lands, treats the state as his household and keeps self-sacrifice in his integrity—he may open an office and appoint aides and clerks.
idiomatic: You hold wisdom within the imperial house, weight of merit and fame, shelter the people in the Way, and spread awe across the realm; you treat the state as family and keep your integrity at cost to yourself—open a chancellery and appoint staff.

literal: " Soon after he was removed as Minister of Works and made chancellor's office.
idiomatic: " Soon after he was stripped of the Ministry of Works and made chancellor.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang, Erzhu Rong wished to harm court gentlemen and then said Yong was plotting rebellion; he met disaster at Heyin.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang came to the throne, Erzhu Rong meant to purge the court and accused Yong of treason; Yong was killed at Heyin.

literal: Posthumously given acting Yellow Battle-Ax and status as prime minister, posthumous title Prince Wenmu.
idiomatic: He was posthumously given the yellow battle-ax and prime-minister rank, with the temple name Prince Wenmu.

literal: Yong's discernment and intent were shallow, and he had no learning; though he stood at the head of court, the temper of the age did not advance him.
idiomatic: Yong's mind was shallow and he had no learning; though he stood first in court, his age did not esteem him.

literal: Because he was kin and exalted and his place was that of chief minister, from Xiping onward, as court governance fell away, he could not hold to the upright and aid correction but only assented.
idiomatic: Kin to the throne and seated as chief minister, from Xiping on he watched government decay and could not hold the line—only nodded assent.

literal: When Prince of Qinghe Yi died and Yuan Cha monopolized government, the great blame of the realm fell on him.
idiomatic: When Prince of Qinghe Yi died and Yuan Cha seized rule, the realm's blame settled on Yong.

literal: His heir Tai, courtesy name Chang, had some reputation in the age.
idiomatic: His heir Tai, courtesy name Chang, enjoyed some repute in his day.

literal: He was Secretariat Gentleman, then transferred to Unhampered Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Pacification-General of the East, and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
idiomatic: He served as secretariat gentleman, then rose to unhampered cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, pacification-general of the east, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

literal: He met disaster together with Yong at the same time.
idiomatic: He fell with Yong on the same day.

literal: Posthumously given Palace Attendant, Special Advance, General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of Taiwei, Inspector of Wuzhou, Prince of Gaoyang, posthumous title Wenxiao.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was palace attendant, special advance, general of agile cavalry, duke of Taiwei, inspector of Wuzhou, prince of Gaoyang, temple name Wenxiao.

literal: His son Bin inherited.
idiomatic: His son Bin inherited.

literal: In the Wuding era he reached office as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era he rose to right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: When Qi received the mandate, his noble rank was reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his rank was reduced as precedent required.

literal: Tai's elder brother Duan, courtesy name Xuanya.
idiomatic: Tai's elder brother Duan, courtesy name Xuanya.

literal: Fine in appearance, he had some acquaintance with books and histories.
idiomatic: Handsome and well favored, he had dipped into books and histories.

literal: He began his career as Cavalier Attendant.
idiomatic: He entered service as cavalier attendant.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Unhampered Attendant, Director of the Court for Dependencies, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Cavalier Attendant.
idiomatic: He rose through unhampered attendant, director of the Court for Dependencies, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and cavalier attendant.

literal: He went out as Pacification-General of the East and Inspector of Qingzhou.
idiomatic: He was sent out as pacification-general of the east and inspector of Qingzhou.

literal: At that time Xiao Yan sent generals to press and threaten Xu and Yang; Duan was made Pacification-General, Bearer of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, commissioner with credentials, Grand Ambassador of the Southeast Route, to dispose military affairs.
idiomatic: Xiao Yan then sent generals against Xu and Yang; Duan was named pacification-general, bearer of the golden seal and purple ribbon, commissioner with credentials, and grand ambassador of the southeast route to command the armies.

literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yanzhou.
idiomatic: When the rebels were crushed he was made general who pacifies the army and inspector of Yanzhou.

literal: Before long Xiao Yan's generals again raided Xu and Yan and pressed the walls of the provincial seat.
idiomatic: Soon Xiao Yan's generals raided Xu and Yan again and besieged the provincial city.

literal: Duan led the civil and military officers of the province in defense and preserved it whole.
idiomatic: Duan led the province's civil and military officers in defense and kept the city intact.

literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ande, [16] with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Ande, [16] with five hundred households.

literal: On return he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Justice.
idiomatic: On his return he was made director of the Ministry of Justice.

literal: He met disaster together with Yong.
idiomatic: He fell with Yong.

literal: Posthumously given General of Chariots and Cavalry, Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was general of chariots and cavalry, ceremonial equal to the three excellencies, and inspector of Xiangzhou.

literal: His son Jun inherited the noble rank.
idiomatic: His son Jun inherited.

literal: When Qi received the mandate, his rank was reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: When Qi took the throne his rank was reduced by precedent.

literal: Tai's younger brother Rui, courtesy name Zizhe.
idiomatic: Tai's younger brother Rui, courtesy name Zizhe.

literal: He lightly disregarded glory and profit and loved to play the zither and read books.
idiomatic: He cared little for rank or gain and loved the zither and books.

literal: He began his career as Unhampered Cavalier Attendant, was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Palace Guard, transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Household, and enfeoffed Prince of Jibei.
idiomatic: He began as unhampered cavalier attendant, became vice director of the Court of the Palace Guard, then vice director of the Court of the Imperial Household, and was enfeoffed prince of Jibei.

literal: He met disaster together with Yong.
idiomatic: He fell with Yong.

literal: Posthumously given General of Chariots and Cavalry, Duke of Works, and Inspector of Yongzhou.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was general of chariots and cavalry, duke of works, and inspector of Yongzhou.

literal: His son Hui, in Putai, inherited the noble rank.
idiomatic: His son Hui inherited in the Putai era.

literal: He began his career as Unhampered Gentleman.
idiomatic: He began as unhampered gentleman.

literal: In the fifth year of Wuding, for plotting rebellion with Yuan Jin and others, he was executed.
idiomatic: In Wuding year five he was executed for plotting rebellion with Yuan Jin and others.

literal: Rui's younger brother Dan, courtesy name Wenfa.
idiomatic: Rui's younger brother Dan, courtesy name Wenfa.

literal: In youth he was clever and had bearing.
idiomatic: Clever as a boy, he carried himself well.

literal: He began his career as Unhampered Gentleman, was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Unhampered Cavalier Attendant.
idiomatic: He began as unhampered gentleman, then became secretariat gentleman and unhampered cavalier attendant.

literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyang, with a fief of three hundred households.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed baron of Xinyang with three hundred households.

literal: He was given the additional title Dragon-Surging General.
idiomatic: He was made dragon-surging general.

literal: He was advanced to Prince of Changle, with a fief of seven hundred households.
idiomatic: He was raised to prince of Changle with seven hundred households.

literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the South, Cavalier Attendant, and Yellow Gate Gentleman.
idiomatic: He became general who pacifies the south, cavalier attendant, and yellow gate gentleman.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Jing he was appointed Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Ceremonial Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: When Emperor Jing came to the throne he was palace attendant, general of chariots and cavalry, ceremonial equal to the three excellencies, and governor of Sizhou.

literal: In the third year of Tianping he died; posthumously given commissioner with credentials, Palace Attendant, Grand Guardian, Duke of Works, Director of the Masters of Writing, his generalship and governorship unchanged, posthumous title Wenxian.
idiomatic: He died in Tianping year three and was posthumously commissioner with credentials, palace attendant, grand guardian, duke of works, and director of the Masters of Writing, with generalship and governorship unchanged; temple name Wenxian.

literal: Having no son, he took Bin's second son Ziliang as heir.
idiomatic: Childless, he took Bin's second son Ziliang as heir.

literal: Dan's younger brother Lecha, Lecha's younger brother Gen, Gen's younger brother Futuo, Futuo's younger brother Amituo, Amituo's younger brother Sengyu, Sengyu's younger brother Juluo.
idiomatic: Dan's younger brothers were Lecha, Gen, Futuo, Amituo, Sengyu, and Juluo.

literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor, Lecha was enfeoffed in Yangping county, Gen in Puyang, Futuo in Wuyang, Amituo in Xinyang, Sengyu in Dunqiu, Juluo in Wei—all as founding barons with fiefs of four hundred households.
idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Lecha was baron of Yangping, Gen of Puyang, Futuo of Wuyang, Amituo of Xinyang, Sengyu of Dunqiu, and Juluo of Wei—each a founding baron with four hundred households.

literal: In Tianping all were appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Cavalier Gentleman.
idiomatic: In Tianping all were made generals who pacify the distant and cavalier gentlemen.

literal: Sengyu fled to Guanxi and his state was abolished.
idiomatic: Sengyu fled west of the passes and his fief was abolished.

literal: The rest, when Qi received the mandate, had their noble ranks reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: The rest, when Qi took the throne, had their ranks reduced by precedent.

literal: Prince of Beihai Xiang, courtesy name Jiyu.
idiomatic: Prince of Beihai Xiang, courtesy name Jiyu.

literal: Fine in bearing and skilled in deportment.
idiomatic: Handsome in bearing and graceful in manner.

literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed and given Palace Attendant and Grand General Who Pacifies the North.
idiomatic: In Taihe year nine he was enfeoffed and made palace attendant and grand general who pacifies the north.

literal: Later he was appointed Grand Master of Splendor and released from palace attendant and general.
idiomatic: Later he was grand master of splendor and relieved of palace attendant and general.

literal: He again held palace attendant concurrently.
idiomatic: He again held palace attendant concurrently.

literal: He followed Gaozu on the southern campaign as Cavalier Attendant.
idiomatic: He followed Gaozu south as cavalier attendant.

literal: When Gaozu toured north from Luoyang, Xiang was constantly in the carriage with Palace Attendant and Prince of Pengcheng Xi, attending at left and right.
idiomatic: When Gaozu rode north from Luoyang, Xiang often shared the carriage with Palace Attendant Xi of Pengcheng, attending at his side.

literal: When they reached the place where Suzong shot the inscription, Gaozu halted the carriage and ordered all his younger brothers and attendant ministers to try shooting near and far; only Xiang's arrow fell short of where Suzong's arrow had landed by more than ten paces.
idiomatic: At the spot where Suzong had shot the inscription stone, Gaozu halted and ordered his brothers and attendants to shoot near and far; only Xiang's arrow fell more than ten paces short of Suzong's mark.

literal: Gaozu praised this, clapped his hands and laughed with delight, and then ordered the inscription carved, composing the text himself.
idiomatic: Gaozu praised him, clapped and laughed with delight, and ordered the inscription carved in his own words.

literal: When the five ranks were first established, his fief was two thousand households.
idiomatic: When the five ranks were first established, his fief was two thousand households.

literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant, then to Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He became palace attendant, then director of the Secretariat.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Xiang acted as Central Army Commander, remained to guard, was given one set of martial pipes and drums, three hundred suits of armor and weapons, and concurrently supervised construction tasks.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign Xiang served as central army commander in the capital, with pipes and drums, three hundred suits of arms, and charge of construction.

literal: Gaozu bestowed on Xiang a sealed letter saying: "Of late what work has the wandering spirit been at?
idiomatic: Gaozu sent Xiang a sealed letter: "Of late what has the wandering spirit been doing?"

literal: In the mounds and the six classics, what is not pastime—well rectify the wind and teachings and make the forbidden guard stern.
idiomatic: "Tombs and the six classics alike should be your pastime; set the guard's discipline straight."

literal: " Later Xiang attended court at the traveling palace and Gaozu received him.
idiomatic: Later Xiang attended at the traveling palace and Gaozu received him.

literal: Xiang congratulated him on pacifying the north bank of the Mian; Gaozu said: "I, because the lands south of the capital are not yet clear, have for a time moved the divine banner; the several cities north of the Mian have all submitted gently—this is the effect of officers and soldiers, not my merit.
idiomatic: Xiang congratulated him on pacifying the Mian's north bank; Gaozu said, "While the capital southlands remain unsettled I have moved the banner for a time; the cities north of the Mian have all submitted—this is the officers' work, not mine."

literal: " Xiang replied: "Your Majesty's virtue surpasses Tang and Yu, your achievement touches Zhou and Han; the wind from the south begins from this.
idiomatic: Xiang answered, "Your virtue surpasses Tang and Yu and your deeds touch Zhou and Han; the south wind begins here."

literal: " When Xiang returned to Luoyang, Gaozu gave him a farewell feast and addressed Xiang: "In former times the Huaiyi rebelled, and therefore there was the campaign of three years;
idiomatic: Returning to Luoyang, Xiang was feasted on departure; Gaozu told him, "When the Huaiyi rebelled, a three-year campaign followed;"

literal: Guifang would not obey, and thus armies were delayed for years.
idiomatic: "when Guifang defied the throne, armies were delayed for years."

literal: How much more do the Jiang and Wu steal the mandate—now ten reign-periods; I must wash clean the southern sea before I speak of returning.
idiomatic: "The Yangtze lands have stolen the mandate these ten reigns; I must scour the southern sea before I return."

literal: This summer I halt here, and therefore meet you; guard the capital well and match what I hold in mind.
idiomatic: "This summer I halt here to see you; guard the capital and keep faith with my intent."

literal: " When Prince of Zhao Jun Gan died, Xiang acted as Governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: When Prince of Zhao Gan died, Xiang acted as governor of Sizhou.

literal: He was appointed General Who Protects the Army and concurrently Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was made general who protects the army and left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Xiang together with the eight seats memorialized: "We consider that robbery and violence are hard to remove, a long-standing pest; bandits make calamity—the chronic sickness of a state.
idiomatic: Xiang and the eight seats memorialized: "Robbery and violence are hard to uproot and long a plague; banditry is a state's chronic sickness."

literal: Therefore the five punishments are applied, yet men still fall into the net of touch-punishment;
idiomatic: "The five punishments are used, yet men still fall into capital nets;"

literal: the Way nearly conquers slaughter, yet the sound of dog-thieves does not cease.
idiomatic: "the Way nearly conquers slaughter, yet petty theft never quiets."

literal: Hence Ban's regulations hang as pattern, called the root of governance; to tighten the net and lift the eyes is the great hinge of policy.
idiomatic: "Ban's code set the pattern called the root of rule; tightening the net and lifting the eyes is policy's great hinge."

literal: We respectfully trace the articles on deprivation of stipend; Ban has completed a full year.
idiomatic: "We have traced the articles on stipend deprivation; a full year has passed since Ban's code."

literal: Yet the magistrates and prefects of the capital are easy to hear for good and ill;
idiomatic: "Yet capital magistrates and prefects are easily judged;"

literal: border prefectures and distant guards sometimes cannot hear and examine clearly—all above and below share feeling and cover for one another in turn.
idiomatic: "border and distant posts sometimes cannot hear cases clearly—high and low cover for one another."

literal: If bandits strike and it is concealed and not reported, or robbery is called theft, or blocking and plundering are made into mere theft, then bandit outbreaks become harder to know and snatching grows worse.
idiomatic: "If raids are hidden, robbery called theft, or blocking and plunder reduced to petty theft, outbreaks grow harder to trace and snatching worsens."

literal: Your subjects jointly deliberate;
idiomatic: "Your subjects jointly deliberate:"

literal: if according to the regulations stipends are cut away, then counties will have no magistrate for a full month;
idiomatic: "if stipends are cut by regulation, counties will lack magistrates within a month;"

literal: if attached articles demote and dismiss, commanderies will lack prefects ripe for a year.
idiomatic: "if attached articles demote and dismiss, commanderies will lack seasoned prefects within a year."

literal: If this regulation must be enforced, it is what is called when laws grow numerous, bandits grow many.
idiomatic: "Enforce this rule and you fulfill the proverb: more laws, more thieves."

literal: In former times Huang Gong changed the wind without cutting stipends;
idiomatic: "Of old Huang Gong changed custom without cutting stipends;"

literal: Zhang and Zhao won praise—would they have feared demotion?
idiomatic: "Zhang and Zhao won praise—did they fear demotion?"
